posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Isolated hero prevents you from affecting any other hero card.

By any means does not affect a hero card, it affects a Villain card, only damage to that card is affected.

Isolated heroes are allowed to affect villain cards, so I don't see why it would not be allowed.

Take down would still work if Legacy was Isolated, and if he wasn't but someone else was the isolated hero would benefit from take down, but Take Down is still a legal play, just like Ground Pound or Hypersonic.

Visionary could still Wrest the Mind or Twist the Ether on a villain card, and while that might benefit another hero it would be allowed, because the effect of the card is on the villain, not the hero.

 

Twist the Ether is a good sample case, by reducing damage or changing type Visionary can greatly affect the Villain-Hero relationship, and affect the Hero target by changing the amount of HP it loses.

By any Means affects a hero card effect by increasing the damage that a villain takes.  Neither effect is directed at a hero card, but both affect hero cards (or effects) secondarily.

posts.cooked:
The word benefit is nowhere on the card.

Your hero and cards cannot affect or be affected by a hero card or effect.

There is nothing in there about heroes not benefiting from your cards effecting a villain target.

If a villain takes reduced damage, that villain is not affecting heroes, the villain is affecting their own cards.  

To interpret that the isolated hero may do nothing that impacts another hero is absurd.

Can you damage a villain target?  That helps other heroes win.

Can you destroy an ongoing card that would deal damage?  That certainly benefits other heroes.

Can you discard a card for Suspicious Malfunction?  If so would the count be different for the isolated vs non-isolated heroes?

What about Threat to the President or concealed betrayal, can the isolated hero be the one who destroys a card?  Can they destroy a card or discard to fulfil the destruction requirement on the card?

None of these situations is the isolated hero or one of their cards affecting another hero, yet they all are beneficial to the other heroes.

If you can't discard toward the (H) cards to destroy Concealed Betrayal, what wording on the actual card Isolated Hero tells you that you can't?

If you can discard, and thus lower the amount of cards the rest of the team needs to discard, then why wouldn't you be able to do the same with other effects of non-hero cards?

The effects of non-hero cards can be affected while you are isolated.  Twist the Ether and Wrest the Mind affecting the effect of a non-hero card is not stopped by Isolated hero.  That the villain card is being affected while effecting a hero target is unimportant to fulfilling the text of the card.

 

Seriously, answer these questions using the text of the card Isolated hero.  Don't just tell me it is explicit and then use wording that isn't on the card to justify your interpretation.  If the card is explicit then use its wording to answer the questions.

Benefiting / affecting can be used interchangibly. Seriously? If you are benefiting from an effect, you are being affected by it. No two ways around that one. I am open to any counter example you can cook up though. "Affecting" wording includes the possibility of excluding effects that could hinder you as well (say Wraith with Micro Targeting is isolated so it would be hurt by Ra having Imbued Fire out). Thats the only difference

I understand what you are saying with the Bounty and its relationship with increasing damage dealt to villain targets. But you have to look at it from an un-isolated heros perspective. Wraith shoots the villain with By Any Means with Razor Ordinance for 3. By Any Mean increases damage dealt to the villain target by 1. Increases whos damage? The hero doing it, of course. Normally, By Any Means would increase the damage Wraith does to the villain by 1. By Any Means, in this example, is an effect coming from an Isolated heros cards/deck. Should Wraith's damage be "affected" by an effect coming directly from an isolated heros cards/deck? You're saying yes? How exactly is Wraith not being affected here again?

To interpret that the isolated hero may do nothing that impacts another hero is absurd.

Absurd? Thats the entire point of the card!!! Thats the EXACT intent.

But you must see the difference between this case and the Any Means Nessesary example. Wraith's damage was being directly affected by the Iso heros card in play. So I see your point with the "benefit" wording, but that minor semantic difference doesn't change the core argument.

I play it that any card that affects non-hero cards (Hypersonic Assualt, By Any Means, Ground Pound, etc) will continue to apply to heroes, as it is directly affecting non-hero cards and not the heroes. While cards that affect heroes/players (Galvanize, Fleet of Foot, Imbued Fire) would not apply to heroes.

posts.cooked:
It seems to me that at least part of the question is about who damage belongs to. Is it:

  1. A property of the damage dealer,
  2. a property of the damage receiver, or
  3. two properties, one belonging to each?

An example:

Wraith, while Galvanized, uses Throwing Knives to damage a villain who has By Any Means played next to them. Under normal circumstances, with no other relevant effects in play, Wraith would deal 3 damage. If Wraith is Isolated, here is how I would interpret the situation for each of the three answers to the question above.

  1. The damage being dealt is Wraith's damage. Since Galvanize and By Any Means directly affect the damage and that damage belongs to Wraith, they cannot be used. The villain takes 1 damage.
  2. The damage being dealt is the villain's damage. Since Galvanize and By Any Means affect the damage and that damage belongs to the villain, they can be used. The villain takes 3 damage. I imagine that most people will agree that this interpretation is not correct.
  3. The damage occurs in two phases. The first phase is Wraith dealing damage. Galvanize affects the damage that Wraith is dealing, so it cannot be used. The Wraith deals one damage in the first phase. The second phase is the villain taking damage. By Any Means affects the damage that the villain is taking, so it can be applied. The total amount of damage dealt to the villain is 2.

I think that 1 and 3 are equally valid interpretations - neither of them is obviously correct, or this discussion would not be happening.
